key_insight: Modality Forcing shows that a pretrained text-to-image model can be post-trained to jointly generate images and depth with a simple recipe, unlocking spatial reasoning without requiring dense depth supervision. The key idea is to reuse the model’s built-in spatial priors and steer them toward scalable 3D-aware generation.
problem_solved: Existing methods for adapting text-to-image models to depth prediction or spatial generation often need dense depth datasets and complicated training pipelines. This paper addresses the need for a simpler, scalable way to learn geometry-aware generation from sparse depth data.
method: Start with a single DiT pretrained on text-to-image data, which already contains strong spatial priors.
Apply a post-training procedure called Modality Forcing to jointly learn image and depth generation from sparse depth supervision.
Use the same model to produce photorealistic scenes with consistent geometry, leveraging modality alignment rather than specialized dense-depth training recipes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a much simpler path to 3D-aware generation and depth-conditioned modeling. It reduces data and engineering complexity, making spatially grounded generative models more practical to train and deploy.

paper_title: Modality Forcing for Scalable Spatial Generation
paper_authors: Bardienus Pieter Duisterhof, Deva Ramanan, Jeffrey Ichnowski, Justin Johnson, Keunhong Park
